heading: Some neurons in image classifiers respond to several unrelated kinds of input
definition: some neurons in image classifiers such as InceptionV1 respond to several unrelated inputs (e.g. cat faces and fronts of cars).
summary: Several independent groups report units with unrelated responses in InceptionV1, Inception V3, ResNets, VGG, AlexNet and ViT encoders, including 31% of 128 randomly sampled units in one ResNet-18. Most of this support comes from selected, qualitative examples, some multi-concept units pair related categories, and no other group has re-examined the original cat/car neuron.

suggested_status.by_scale: Size buckets cannot separate the evidence (counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size = not stated 30, <1B 1, 1-10B 1). R2 across vision models of unstated size: CNN classifiers (ResNet, VGG, AlexNet, Inception V1/V3) and ViT encoders. No studies at toy scale, 10-100B or >100B.
suggested_status.reason: The original (DOI:10.23915/distill.00024.001#R1) shows one InceptionV1 neuron (4e:55), re-presented from Feature Visualization 2017, with no count. No tested study shares an author with an original (counts: versions.V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0). Other groups report units with unrelated responses in InceptionV1 (arXiv:2211.12312, qualitative; arXiv:2406.03662, early vision via SAEs), Inception V3 (arXiv:2304.09707), ResNet-18 (arXiv:2006.14032: 31% of 128 randomly sampled units), ResNet-50 (arXiv:2404.06453: a few hundred of 2048), and in ViT encoders (arXiv:2504.02821). counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 26, limits_scope.studies = 3, challenges.studies = 0; tested_by_review_class.reviewed = 9; tested_with_controls = 18. The limits: some multi-concept units pair related categories (arXiv:1711.05611), and one measure is a contribution, not a response (arXiv:2203.14196). Most support is from selected, qualitative examples. The canonical cat/car neuron has not been re-examined by anyone else.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) Would a re-analysis of InceptionV1 4e:55 with SAEs or attribution clustering find one shared feature? That bears on the canonical example and on V6. (2) What share of InceptionV1 units mix unrelated inputs, measured with a stated unrelatedness criterion and a null baseline? (3) Do the reported shares hold when top-k, activation range, cluster count and the embedding model or judge are varied? (4) Do intervention results show that the network uses each of a unit's unrelated responses?

source.title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
source.authors: Chris Olah; Nick Cammarata; Ludwig Schubert; Gabriel Goh; Michael Petrov; Shan Carter

original_result.setup: They used feature visualization and dataset examples to show what activates one InceptionV1 neuron, 4e:55 in layer mixed4e.
original_result.result: Neuron 4e:55 responds to cat faces, fronts of cars and cat legs. It is a single illustrated example, with no count of how common such neurons are.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: 31% of sampled ResNet-18 units responded to unrelated concepts.
Individual InceptionV1 neurons looked highly polysemantic; one responded to dog noses and metal poles.
Two AlexNet filters responded to unrelated pairs such as terrier faces and metal cylinders.
Authors report most analysed Inception V3 neurons were polysemantic; one responded to peacocks and vans.
Some DINO ResNet-50 features strongly activated on unrelated images like mushrooms and water towers.
Selected CLIP ViT-B-32 neurons mixed unrelated concepts like limousines, suits and bullmastiffs.
Sparse autoencoders split selected InceptionV1 early-vision neurons into several distinct features.
A few hundred of 2048 ResNet-50 neurons had top-activating images that split into semantically separate groups.
A ResNet-50 channel responded most strongly to both digital clocks and cauliflower.
Selected CLIP-ViT-L/14 units responded to several shapes, colours and positions.
A channel in ResNet-50's last stage had top-activating image patches split between columns and foliage.
Some ResNet152 channels mixed unrelated concepts, such as peppers, deer, dogs and a truck.
Whole CLIP-RN50x16 neurons had looser top-image clusters than their per-attention-head components, suggesting polysemanticity.
Hand-picked DINOv2-B/14 units' top images mixed unrelated concepts like shoes and clownfish.
Baseline models trained only with cross-entropy had units firing on unrelated classes like frogs, ships, airplanes.
Custom CNN channels co-activated for mitochondria and lysosomes in iPSC-neuron microscopy images.
A ResNet18 neuron detected animals, vehicles and vases, according to MILAN's automatic text description.
A ResNet-18 penultimate neuron's top images spanned water jets, bridges and animal faces.
CIFAR-10 ResNet50 neurons were less coherent than directions found by K-Means clustering, on every metric.
A ResNet-50 neuron responded strongly to snow and skiing, and weakly to dog-like animals.
Humans found directions from dictionary learning more visually coherent than single ResNet50 and VGG16 neurons.
Authors report several polysemantic VGG-16 penultimate units that play multiple roles in the model's decisions.
Two hand-picked neurons in NeSyViT, a neuro-symbolic ViT, responded to mixed features without clear concept selectivity.
All individual ViT encoder units had chance-level similarity scores: their activating images were dissimilar.
A substantial share of OpenCLIP, DINOv2 and diffusion-transformer neurons was judged polysemantic.
All inspected CLIP ViT-L MLP neurons looked polysemantic, typically mixing 3–4 unrelated features.
An underwater neuron's two image groups showed related facets, not unrelated inputs.
The two multi-concept GoogLeNet units shown paired related categories, such as horses and dogs.
A VGG19 neuron contributed to birds and cars, but with opposite signs.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: The canonical example itself: no study other than the original re-examines InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 or the cat-face/car-front mixture, with feature visualization or newer tools (SAEs, attribution clustering).
untested.basis: Nearly every tested study's 'untested parts of V1' line names InceptionV1's cat/car neuron (e.g. arXiv:2006.14032, arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2304.09707, arXiv:2406.03662). counts: versions.V1.original_sources_linked = [DOI:10.23915/distill.00024.001]; versions.V1.studies_with_untested_parts = 28.

untested.what: A share of polysemantic units in InceptionV1/GoogLeNet with a stated criterion for 'unrelated': the Inception-family studies are qualitative (arXiv:2211.12312), cover early vision only (arXiv:2406.03662), report 'majority' with no denominator (arXiv:2304.09707 r7), or give no count (arXiv:1711.05611).
untested.basis: Pack 'untested parts' and 'problems' lines of arXiv:2211.12312, arXiv:2406.03662, arXiv:2304.09707, arXiv:1711.05611. counts: versions.V1.studies_by_family = 'other or not stated' 31, so the counts cannot split vision architectures.

untested.what: An intervention test (ablation, patching, steering) showing that the network uses a unit's responses to each unrelated input; CoE's untested line names causal tests per channel.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.coverage_by_operation has only evaluation, measurement, probing and training; versions.V1.main_rows_by_operation = measurement 92, evaluation 6, probing 2, training 1. Pack 'untested parts of V1' line of arXiv:2503.15234.

untested.what: How the share changes with model size in supervised image classifiers; the only scale result is in OpenCLIP, DINOv2 and diffusion transformers (arXiv:2606.03990, figure only). No evidence at 10-100B or above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size = not stated 30, <1B 1, 1-10B 1; versions.V1.coverage_by_operation has no scaling key.

wording_issues.issue: Much of the support comes from vision models that are not classifiers: diffusion transformers (arXiv:2606.03990 R5, R6; the verdict notes they are generative vision models), self-supervised DINO ResNet-50 (arXiv:2307.10504), and contrastive or self-supervised encoders CLIP ViT-L/14, SigLIP, AIMv2 and WebSSL MAE (arXiv:2504.02821).

Some units counted as neurons are not native activation-function neurons: in arXiv:2504.02821 they are CLS residual-stream/output dimensions of ViTs (verdict reason); in arXiv:2602.12403 they are dimensions of an added embedding layer, not backbone neurons; in arXiv:2505.06745 they sit in a newly trained sparse concept layer.

Several studies measure a unit's output effect, not its activation response. arXiv:2203.14196 measures Shapley contribution to concept classifiers (neuron 199 activates on birds, deactivates on car wheels; r1). arXiv:2406.04341 decomposes second-order effects into positive and negative text terms (e.g. dolphin negative in T5-974-words). arXiv:2509.19943 ranks top images by contribution norm (r8).

Several reported mixtures are related, or their unrelatedness is not established. GoogLeNet units pair horses/dogs and white ellipsoids/jets, which the authors call generalizations (arXiv:1711.05611 r1, r2). CLIP ViT-B-32 neurons 4, 391 and 2137 have positive terms sharing winter, wood and food/sweets themes (arXiv:2406.04341, partial). CoE concept 1681 is dominated by face/mask with minor extras (arXiv:2503.15234 r2, partial). Toy-shape affinities are confounded by co-occurrence in multi-object images, with no baseline (arXiv:2508.16652 R1).

The statement gives no share, and the reported shares differ widely by setting. 31% of 128 randomly sampled units are polysemantic after manual inspection of length-10 compositional explanations (ResNet-18 Places365 final conv layer; arXiv:2006.14032 r1). A few hundred of 2048 neurons (ImageNet ResNet-50 penultimate layer; arXiv:2404.06453 r1). All inspected MLP neurons (CLIP ViT Large; lw:bCtbuWraqYTDtuARg r1). arXiv:2504.02821 gives scores, not a share. With MS computed from DINOv2 ViT-B embeddings, the highest raw-unit MS is 0.01 in CLIP ViT-L/14-336px layers 11, 17, 22, 23 and last, where best = worst (r1-r5). It is also 0.01 in the last layer of CLIP ViT-L/14-336px, SigLIP SoViT-400m, AIMv2 L/14 and WebSSL MAE-300m (r29-r32).

method_sensitivity.factor: Activation range and number of top-activating inputs examined
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2405.06855: ResNet-50 layer4 neuron 136 shows snow/skiing at high activations and dog-like animals at lower ones (R31); the measured share of causal impact depends strongly on the fraction of highest-activating inputs examined and varies by layer. arXiv:2606.03990: VLM-judged monosemanticity rates decrease as more top-activating images are shown, stabilising around k = 20. arXiv:2605.31304: the probing dataset and top-k choice determine which concepts can be extracted. arXiv:2310.11431: in-silico psychophysics accuracy drops as queries move to central activation quantiles (R3).

method_sensitivity.factor: Unit analysed (neuron axes vs learned directions or path components)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2411.03993: dictionary directions score above neuron axes in all three human experiments (ResNet50 83.5% vs 78.8% and 85.1% vs 76.2%; VGG16 81.5% vs 77.1%). arXiv:2310.11431: K-Means directions are more coherent than neurons; most neuron pairs lower the index, though some sums are more interpretable (not in rows). arXiv:2307.10504: individual-feature image sets are diverse while selected feature groups give coherent sets, e.g. pair 1643/2006 jointly selects hot air balloons (not in rows). arXiv:2509.19943 (CLIP-RN50x16 final layer, Fig. 3, no values in the text): by raw count there are far more low-inertia (less-polysemantic) neuron-head pairs than neurons, with ~147,000 pairs vs ~3,072 neurons (48 heads). The pairs are neuron x attention-pooling-head path components, not learned directions, and the authors say they remain polysemantic (r8).

method_sensitivity.factor: Clustering settings used to split a unit's top inputs
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2404.06453: separation depends on clustering method (PURE vs activations), number of clusters, architecture and evaluation embedding; with 2 clusters, neurons #1177 and #141 carry three semantics (r12, r13); CLIP and attribution clusterings disagree. arXiv:2508.16950: the K̂ search range of 2-5 forces at least 2 clusters (r17, cannot_determine); PSI ranking stability varies with the number of top patches K; D-score agreement varies with the CLIP text head (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.21). arXiv:2304.09707: the distance threshold dmax changes concept granularity and can merge or split clusters.

method_sensitivity.factor: Embedding model or explainer used to score coherence
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2504.02821 (CLIP ViT-L raw units): with DINOv2 ViT-B as the embedding encoder, best = worst MS 0.01 (r1; Table A5). With CLIP ViT-B as the encoder, mean MS is 0.4812-0.4840 (Table A3) and best/worst 0.50/0.47 (Table A6) (not in rows). The text states no chance level. SAE gains over raw units are smaller with CLIP ViT-B (App. E.2), but human alignment scores differ by at most 0.04 between the two encoders in every MS-distance bin (Table A1). arXiv:2503.15234: CPE has a high floor: the uniform lobster channel (concept 141, Table S8) scores 0.70 after padding (r6 verdict fix). CPE trends also differ across relevance-, activation- and mutual-information-based XAI methods (mutual-information CPE for ResNet152 only).

arXiv:2508.16950: ResNet-50 layer4 PSI distribution is above layer3 (r9); top layer3 units respond to textures and patterns, layer4 to object parts or whole objects (not in rows). arXiv:2201.11114: in ResNet18, neurons with large semantic differences are more prevalent in later layers (not in rows, Figure 4). arXiv:2503.15234: average non-overlapping semantic atoms per concept are 18.3 at stage 3 and 12.7 at stage 4 (r4, r5), but the verdict marks both cannot_determine because atom counts mix colours, textures and materials with objects.

arXiv:2006.14032: vision mean IoU rises from 0.059 at formula length 1 to 0.099 at length 10; the study does not report whether this changes the polysemantic share. arXiv:1711.05611: interpretability changes with the activation threshold τ, and only each unit's top-ranked concept is kept, so a unit detecting several concepts is labelled once (not in rows, Section 2.2).

arXiv:2501.05398 (polysemanticity score in %, ImageNet subset, no uncertainty reported): with L1 activation-sparsity λ=80, ResNet34 goes 91.5→67.0 and VGG-13 (BN) 84.8→71.8, but ResNet50 only 89.3→87.7 and VGG-13 83.3→83.2 (Supp Tab G.2). Dropout lowers only VGG-13 (BN) (84.7→78.4); the other models move by 0.4 or less (Tab G.1). Task complexity: ResNet34 +6.6, the others about ±2, with VGG-13 down (Tab G.3). Training epochs 39-399: about 1 point or less, except ResNet50 (1.5-2.7, epochs 39-199 only; Tab G.5). Among pre-trained ImageNet models, narrow ResNet18 and ViTs score higher (Sec 4.4.2, Fig 5b, no numbers). arXiv:1711.05611: interpretability changes with architecture, training dataset, dropout, batch normalisation and basis rotation. arXiv:2606.03990: the non-Rosetta monosemantic fraction falls and the Rosetta fraction rises with model scale (figure only). These bear mainly on V5.
